mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million units signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not statistically significant at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not robust to a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not significant at the 10% level.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI above their respective 5-year averages for three consecutive months signals a dual tightening in monetary and price stability policy, which increases real discount rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5-year avg AND CPIAUCSL > 5-year avg for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not statistically significant at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 5% while personal income growth (PAYEMS YoY) remains below 2% signals a shift from consumption to saving, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 5% AND PAYEMS YoY < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not significant at the 10% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals a significant labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not robust across three rolling 5-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 5% for three consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related industries and supports broader economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change > 5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the positive rank IC is not significant at the 5% level.
